## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

The CLI should honor `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` so CI can apply exclusions through the environment.

## Changes

The pull request adds and documents a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that skips files by basename and logs skips in verbose mode. It adds tests for argument parsing, file collection, and archive contents.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the exclusion default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and no `--exclude` argument, the parser returns an empty list. `.agents/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` requires that “Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable.” — CI jobs that configure exclusions through the environment archive files they intended to skip.

## Suggestions

- cli/main.py:33 — tests — Cover basename matching in subdirectories — For `nested/skip.log` and the glob `skip*.log`, the basename matches and the source-relative path fails to match. All exclusion tests use files directly under the source directory, so they cannot distinguish those behaviors. — A switch to source-relative matching could include excluded files from subdirectories while the existing tests still pass. — Fix: Extend `test_main_leaves_excluded_files_out_of_the_archive` with a nested file and a glob anchored at the start of its basename.
